clue.text: Change for the better. Regulation of vehicle movement

definitions.text: Change for the better. Regulation of vehicle movement

parts.words: Change for the better. Regulation of vehicle movement
parts.note: roadside signals keep switching colour, and the first sentence plays on that switching as though it were reform

explanation.surface: A slogan of improvement followed by a dry note on traffic law.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals at junctions control when cars stop and go, which is regulating vehicle movement.

clue.text: Nurses not needed to bind the cuts of these farm workers

definitions.text: Nurses not needed to bind the cuts of these farm workers

parts.words: Nurses not needed to bind the cuts of these farm workers
parts.note: cuts here are the harvested stalks, bound into sheaves by machine, not wounds needing bandages

explanation.surface: A remark that injured harvest hands can manage without medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvest labourers who cut grain are named for that cutting; old machines were reaper-binders.

clue.text: Dooms merrymakings, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for merrymakings is only heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: fetes are festive celebrations

explanation.surface: Gloomy news that the parties are doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's destinies or dooms are their lots in life, often unhappy ones.

clue.text: High water is too hard for navigation

definitions.text: High water is too hard for navigation

parts.words: High water is too hard for navigation
parts.note: high water means water standing tall above the sea, and frozen solid it endangers ships

explanation.surface: A sailor's complaint that a flood tide makes steering difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mountain of frozen water rises high above the waves and is a hazard to shipping.

clue.text: Lunatic clouts a pest

indicators.note: a lunatic arrangement is a crazy one, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A madman hits an annoying person.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming insects that strip crops are a classic agricultural plague.

clue.text: Untried combative token; a fruit

parts.note: a green recruit is inexperienced or untried
a gage was a glove thrown down as a pledge of combat

explanation.surface: A list of odd items: an inexperienced fighting pledge and a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of plum with greenish skin, so it is a variety of fruit.

clue.text: Oral test by the domestic science mistress?

definitions.text: Oral test by the domestic science mistress?

parts.words: Oral test by the domestic science mistress?
parts.note: an oral test sounds like a spoken exam, but here it is a test by mouth of cooked food

explanation.surface: A school cookery teacher sets a spoken examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling food by mouth to judge it is literally an oral test.

clue.text: Begin with left half. Surprise, surprise!

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: only the first half of the word left is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to start with the left side, followed by an exclamation of amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a sudden shock is to surprise them, a near synonym.

clue.text: Educational authority, traditionally black!

parts.note: the governing body of schools shares its name with the classroom slate that was traditionally black

explanation.surface: A remark that school administrators are traditionally gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A former local body running schools in Britain shares its name with a classroom blackboard.

clue.text: How the fold leaves the paper, as it were

definitions.text: How the fold leaves the paper, as it were

parts.words: How the fold leaves the paper, as it were
parts.note: folding a sheet leaves a line in it, describing the paper's state afterwards

explanation.surface: A description of paper after it has been folded.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper that has been folded is left marked with lines, or wrinkled.

clue.text: Man shot lady over poet

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are knocked over and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A grim headline about a man shooting a woman over a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh writer of Under Milk Wood was a famous poet.

clue.text: More than one foot back

parts.note: the rear parts of more than one foot, not a distance of over a foot

explanation.surface: A measurement of something set slightly over a foot behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded rear parts of the feet are the backs of more than one foot.

clue.text: It's vital to see Latin's translated

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the word Latin with its s kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A teacher stressing that Latin must be understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absolutely necessary is vital, a synonym.

clue.text: Getting out got us in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are disturbed and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A confession that an escape attempt landed people in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Expelling or forcing someone out is getting them out.

clue.text: Those who complain

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Those who complain (9)' for IMPATIENT: appears cut short; no wordplay or fitting definition for the singular adjective.

clue.text: It's for professional speakers

parts.note: the specialised vocabulary that people in a profession speak among themselves

explanation.surface: Something seemingly reserved for paid orators.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical terms used within a trade or profession form its special language.

clue.text: Old fliers with exaggerated feelings of self-importance

definitions.meaning: small non-rigid airships of the early twentieth century
Colonel Blimp, a cartoon character, gave his name to pompous reactionary people

explanation.definitionFit: Early airships bore this name, and so do pompous, self-important old reactionaries after a cartoon colonel.

clue.text: One little devil per man. Charge?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
each means for every person

explanation.surface: A question of how much to charge each person for an imp.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse an official of wrongdoing is to charge them.

clue.text: Spot his emblem without me. That's odd!

indicators.note: the letters are made odd, rearranged, once the second group is taken from them

explanation.surface: Someone noticing a badge with a letter pair missing and finding it strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without me' takes ME from HISEMBLEM, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish is a mark or spot on skin or a surface.

clue.text: Frequently a way to get round 24ac

definitions.text: Frequently a way to get round 24ac

parts.words: Frequently a way to get round 24ac
parts.note: getting round foes means surrounding them in a siege, not evading them

explanation.surface: Advice on how to circumvent opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround a town or army with troops is to lay siege to the foes.

clue.text: In the Tiber.I and others find a subject of the Roman Empire

definitions.text: a subject of the Roman Empire

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Searching around the Roman river for one of the empire's peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal formed a peninsula within Rome's empire, so its people were Roman subjects.

clue.text: Figure it's representation in the round, as it were

definitions.text: Figure it's representation in the round, as it were

parts.words: Figure it's representation in the round, as it were
parts.note: a sculpted figure is a representation in the round, carved to be seen from all sides

explanation.surface: Musing on a figure shown in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional sculpture of a figure is a representation in the round.

clue.text: Desires peeps at it. Pervert!

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or distort, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A voyeur scolded as a pervert for peeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Cravings or desires are appetites, a synonym.

clue.text: Right in a ray fish

indicators.note: puts the letter for right inside the word for a ray

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A ray fish described as correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Tree at home in sandy soil, it's said

indicators.note: signals that the word for sandy soil is spoken to give its sound-alike

parts.note: a beach is a stretch of sandy ground by the sea

explanation.surface: A tree said to flourish in sandy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-barked deciduous tree common in Europe.

clue.text: Lovers say it is the most expensive

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment between sweethearts
superlative of dear in its sense of costly

explanation.definitionFit: Lovers call each other this endearment, and it is also the superlative of dear, meaning costliest.

clue.text: No pacifists, but against us getting involved in war

definitions.text: No pacifists, but against us getting involved in war

parts.words: No pacifists, but against us getting involved in war
parts.note: people who are against us in war, not campaigners against war

explanation.surface: A note on anti-war people opposing involvement in conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents in war are those against us, the foe.

clue.text: Paint the wheel ordered for a stall at the fete

definitions.text: for a stall at the fete

indicators.note: the letters are ordered, put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions to paint a wheel for a stall at a village fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted household items sold at a fete's bric-a-brac stall go by this name.
